bank: EYES AND EARS -- THE GLITCH TAXONOMY FOR THIS GAME
note: DRAFT MATERIAL, NEVER WIRED INTO THE GAME. One line each: what it looks like, and how a machine finds it on a screenshot of OUR game -- 45-degree pixel art drawn on a canvas inside an iframe, on a phone. STATUS says whether the machine can do it TODAY (running), whether it needs a harness that does not exist yet, or whether only a person can answer.
grounding: The split of temporal and non-temporal failures is Lewis, Whitehead and Wardrip-Fruin (FDG 2010). The visual classes are the ones industry detectors actually train on (EA SEED's CNN glitch detector; GlitchBench): corrupted, missing, stretched and placeholder textures, clipping, floating, lighting. Everything below is those ideas translated into what our game is.

glitches.name: nothing there
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a screen that is one flat colour: black, or the shell's ground, with no game on it
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: the dominant colour bucket covers more than 85% of a sampled grid, or no canvas over 200x400 exists in any frame

glitches.name: off the glass
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a control sitting below the bottom of the phone, or past its right edge, that no scroll can reach
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: every visible leaf element's rect PLUS its frame's offset in the phone, against 390x844, skipping anything inside a scrollable box

glitches.name: cut text
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a button that loses its last word; a caption chopped at the right edge
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: scrollWidth greater than clientWidth on an element whose overflow is not scrollable
glitches.found: CHARACTER bench SHOULDERS cut by 14px; MAP caption cut by 484px

glitches.name: he cannot read it
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a label or a line of dialogue the same brightness as what is behind it
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: the DOM says WHERE the words are, the finished picture says what they look like: WCAG contrast between the darkest and lightest tenth inside the text's rectangle, 4.5:1 floor for body, 3:1 for large. A scrim drawn OVER the text is invisible to the styles and obvious to the picture
glitches.found: 38 boxes under the floor on the first screen with the morning card up (OUTFIT 1.03:1); 7 still under it with the card gone

glitches.name: a dead flat patch
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a rectangle of one exact colour where art should be: a missing tile, an unpainted hole, a panel that never drew
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: 48px blocks whose pixels are all one colour, joined into patches, reported over 6 blocks. Flat is legal in pixel art, so the number is reported and a person rules

glitches.name: the picture does not reach the glass
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a black band along an edge; a letterboxed world on a phone that has no letterbox
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: count flat single-colour rows or columns inward from each edge
glitches.found: the CUTSCENE screen carries a 94px band under the picture

glitches.name: the page threw
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a screen that renders anyway while something underneath it is broken
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: pageerror on either surface, plus failed fetches counted separately

glitches.name: the world is a photograph
glitches.what_it_looks_like: nothing moves: no wind, no person, no light change
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: two frames N seconds apart with no input; 0.00% of pixels moved is a still image
glitches.found: three demo frames eighteen seconds apart are byte-identical

glitches.name: the same block, pasted
glitches.status: NEEDS THE DATA, NOT THE PICTURE
glitches.what_it_looks_like: one apartment block repeated straight down a column of the map
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: NOT from the screenshot. Measured 9/5: a lattice autocorrelation scores the MAP screen 0.21, the walked game 0.22 and a grid of judge cards 0.25 -- it cannot tell a copy-pasted city from a correct grid. The question belongs to the table the map is generated FROM, where a repeat is an exact match and not a correlation

glitches.name: a sprite through a wall
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a body drawn over a wall it should be behind, or standing in it
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: the world knows where its walls and its bodies are; ask the game for both and compare, rather than asking the picture. A pixel test cannot separate 'behind' from 'inside'

glitches.name: wrong draw order
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a person behind a car that is behind the person; a roof over a body on the near side
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: same as G-10: the sort key the renderer used, checked against the sort key the geometry implies

glitches.name: a seam between tiles
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a one-pixel line of the wrong colour where two tiles meet
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: on the tile grid, compare each tile's edge row against its neighbour's touching row; a seam is a step that appears at the grid pitch and nowhere else

glitches.name: a frame popping
glitches.what_it_looks_like: one frame of an animation that jumps and comes back
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: frame-to-frame diff across a clip: a spike between two low numbers is a pop. Needs the clip captured as frames, which the screenshot pass does not do yet

glitches.name: a floating window
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a panel with nothing under it, or a card whose edge hangs over the world with no ground
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: a panel rect whose four edges all sit over live world pixels with no shadow, border or ground row

glitches.name: the placeholder shipped
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a checkerboard, a magenta box, a debug label left in a shipped screen
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: a colour match for the known placeholder set plus a checkerboard autocorrelation at small pitch; industry detectors call this 'placeholder texture' and it is the cheapest class to catch

glitches.name: two of the same game
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a second logo, a second panel style, a tab that looks like a different app
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: it cannot. A machine can put the two screens side by side; a person says whether they are one game
glitches.found: the gold wordmark on the front door against the white one struck through in magenta on the fight

glitches.name: art from another world
glitches.what_it_looks_like: furniture, food or a room from a different kind of game
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: it cannot. This is the 9/4 compare law's job, and E7 is the scoring sheet for it

glitches.name: the wrong thing is loud
glitches.what_it_looks_like: a decorative element louder than the thing the player must act on
glitches.how_a_machine_finds_it: a machine can rank contrast and size; only a person can say which element should have won
